tldr: MOBA is an MLLM-based mobile assistant that uses adaptive planning with reflection for error recovery and a multifaceted memory module to dynamically adjust task plans based on real-time GUI context and execution capacity.
contributions: Proposes an adaptive planning module with a reflection mechanism for error recovery that dynamically adjusts plans based on GUI environment and action executor capacity
Develops a multifaceted memory module with five components (Task, App, Page, Action, User Memory) providing hierarchical memory support
Introduces MOBBENCH, a dataset of 50 tasks across 10 Chinese applications with varying difficulty levels including cross-application tasks
methods: MOBA employs an adaptive planning workflow where a Global Agent decomposes tasks into sub-goals and a Reflection Module reviews feasibility before execution. A Local Agent executes actions on the device, after which the Reflection Module assesses outcomes and triggers task revision or further decomposition upon failure. The multifaceted Memory Module stores hierarchical experiences across five categories to support both planning and execution, with warm-up initialization using expert experiences.
results: On MOBBENCH (50 tasks), MOBA achieved a Complete Rate of 28/50, Milestone Score of 88 (66.2%), and Execution Efficiency of 3.44 steps per milestone, outperforming AppAgent (6/50 CR) and MobileAgent v2 (17/50 CR). On Android Arena, MOBA achieved success rates of 0.783 on single-app tasks (+2.4% over GPT-4) and 0.714 on cross-app tasks (+14.3% over GPT-4). Ablation studies showed the Plan module alone contributed more than the Memory module alone, with combined modules yielding the best performance.
limitations: Overall task completion rates are relatively low for all agents due to mobile interface complexity
MOBA tends to execute redundant actions after task completion, complicating automated evaluation
GPT-4 misclassified 11.8% of tasks when used as an automated evaluator compared to human checking
